abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \dots, \zeta(s)$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $\zeta(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.
hook: Proved: more odd zeta values must be irrational, improving the count by a sqrt(log log s) factor.
summary: For large odd s, the authors show at least 2.78 sqrt(s loglog s / log s) of the values zeta(3) through zeta(s) are irrational, beating the previous bound by a slowly growing factor. The proof merges earlier elimination, hypergeometric and Hankel determinant methods. It still cannot identify which values are irrational.
title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
